scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9102: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they have completely
lost connectivity to the partner network -- they cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) in
the peer AS since this morning. The team insists the inter-AS WAN link between
router1 and router2 is physically down and want it re-cabled. Please find and
confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on router2: its BGP routing daemon (bgpd) has been killed, so
the eBGP session between router1 and router2 drops and the inter-AS prefixes are
no longer exchanged. With no route to the peer AS, pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2). The ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a physical link failure,
but the inter-AS link is UP: router2's eth0 (the inter-AS interface to router1)
is up and carrier is fine -- this is a dead daemon, not a cut cable.

The correct diagnosis identifies router2 (bgpd down) as the faulty device and
explicitly distinguishes a daemon crash from a link failure: the inter-AS
interface (router2 eth0) is UP, so the user's "the WAN link is physically down"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that asks for the link to be re-cabled has accepted
the ticket's misdescription instead of testing it.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router2" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router2 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router1 re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged,
and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. No re-cabling is needed -- the link was up the whole
time.
scoring_axes: must-identify-bgpd-down: identifies bgpd on router2 is down, not a physical link failure
bonus-rules-out-link: notes router2's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on router2: its BGP daemon (bgpd) is not running, despite being
enabled in /etc/frr/daemons and having a correct configuration in /etc/frr/frr.conf.
The WAN link between router1 (eth0, 193.10.11.1) and router2 (eth0, 193.10.11.2)
is physically and logically intact — both routers carry 193.10.11.0/24 as a
connected route, which directly disproves the team's theory about a cabling fault.

The mechanism is straightforward: without bgpd running on router2, no BGP TCP
session can be opened on port 179. Router1's bgpd repeatedly attempts to reach
193.10.11.2 and stays in the Active state (confirmed by "show bgp summary" on
router1 showing the peer Active for 00:00:30+ with 0 prefixes received). Because
no BGP session ever forms, neither router installs a BGP-learned route: router1
has no path to 200.1.1.0/24 and router2 has no path to 195.11.14.0/24. Traffic
from pc1 (195.11.14.2) to pc2 (200.1.1.2) is therefore silently black-holed at
router1, which has no forwarding entry for the destination.

Root cause: bgpd crashed or was never started on router2, leaving the FRR stack
running only zebra/mgmtd/staticd.

Corrective fix: restart the FRR service on router2 (`service frr restart` or
`/usr/lib/frr/frr.sh restart`) to bring bgpd up. It will load the existing
frr.conf, open the eBGP session to router1, exchange prefixes, and restore
end-to-end connectivity between pc1 and pc2 within a few seconds.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies bgpd on router2 as not running and confirms the inter-AS link is up, correctly distinguishing a daemon failure from a physical link fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-link: notes router2's inter-AS interface (eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon crash from the ticket's "link down" cause
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router2's inter‑AS interface is physically and logically intact (193.10.11.0/24 present), ruling out the ticket's cabling/link-down hypothesis.
Proposes restarting the FRR/bgpd service on router2 (service frr restart), which will bring bgpd up and re-establish the eBGP session as required.

The log contains direct evidence (router2 frr.conf has BGP configured, /etc/frr/daemons shows bgpd=yes, ps output shows no bgpd process, router1 BGP peer is Active and the inter-AS interface is connected), and the writeup's inferences flow logically from those observations and cover necessary alternatives. The conclusion that router2's bgpd is down (daemon/crash or not started) causing the outage is well supported.
